title: Is it possible to use one Hive Metastore with different hive catalogs in Spark (Iceberg)?
question:
What I have:

  1. Holding's industries: fintech, telco, plants

  2. Hive Metastore (with PostgreSQL) docker deployment available on thrift://hms-host:9083.

    I've manually inserted additional 3 catalog records into CTLGS table (postgres):

    CTLG_ID NAME DESC LOCATION_URI
    1 hive Default catalog for Hive file:/user/hive/warehouse
    3 fintech Catalog for Fintech s3a://fintech
    2 telco Catalog for Telco s3a://telco
    4 plants Catalog for Plants s3a://plants

    DBS table content:

    DB_ID DESC DB_LOCATION_URI NAME OWNER_NAME OWNER_TYPE CTLG_NAME
    1 Default Hive database file:/user/hive/warehouse default public ROLE hive
    6 Created by me Trino schema s3a://fintech/digipays digipays carl.cox USER fintech
    7 Created by me Trino schema s3a://telco/worldonline worldonline carl.cox USER telco
    8 Created by me Trino schema s3a://plants/plastix meters_bus carl.cox USER plants
    10 Created by collegaue from Spark somehow s3a://corporate/sparkk.db sparkk john.digweed USER hive

  3. Minio cluster available on https://my-minio-host:9000 endpoint with access and secret keys and 3 buckets: s3a://fintech s3a://telco s3a://plants

What I'm trying to achieve:

Write simple PySpark (3.5.1) code with correct configuration that will "see" and show list of available catalogs according to my catalogs in Hive Metastore (fintech, telco, plants)

My following simple PySpark code snippet returns only default and sparkk databases (they are both related to hive catalog), but supposed to return worldonline:

import pyspark
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

CATALOG_CLASS   = "org.apache.iceberg.spark.SparkCatalog"
CATALOG_TYPE    = "hive"
HMS_URI         = "thrift://hms-host:9083"
AWS_ENDPOINT    = "https://my-minio-host:9000"
AWS_ACCESS_KEY  = "123"
AWS_SECRET_KEY  = "12345678"

spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("IcebergHiveMetastoreIntegration") \
    .config("spark.sql.catalog.fintech",                     CATALOG_CLASS) \
    .config("spark.sql.catalog.telco",                       CATALOG_CLASS) \
    .config("spark.sql.catalog.plants",                      CATALOG_CLASS) \
    .config("spark.sql.catalog.fintech.type",                CATALOG_TYPE) \
    .config("spark.sql.catalog.telco.type",                  CATALOG_TYPE) \
    .config("spark.sql.catalog.plants.type",                 CATALOG_TYPE) \
    .config("spark.sql.catalog.fintech.uri",                 HMS_URI) \
    .config("spark.sql.catalog.telco.uri",                   HMS_URI) \
    .config("spark.sql.catalog.plants.uri",                  HMS_URI) \
    .config("spark.sql.catalog.fintech.default-namespace",   "fintech") \
    .config("spark.sql.catalog.telco.default-namespace",     "telco") \
    .config("spark.sql.catalog.plants.default-namespace",    "plants") \
    .config("spark.hadoop.fs.s3a.endpoint",                     AWS_ENDPOINT) \
    .config("spark.hadoop.fs.s3a.access.key",                   AWS_ACCESS_KEY) \
    .config("spark.hadoop.fs.s3a.secret.key",                   AWS_SECRET_KEY) \
    .config("spark.hadoop.fs.s3a.path.style.access", "true") \
    .getOrCreate()

spark.sql("USE telco")
spark.sql("SHOW CATALOGS").show()
spark.sql("SHOW NAMESPACES").show()
spark.sql("SHOW DATABASES").show()

Output:

+-------------+
|      catalog|
+-------------+
|        telco|
|spark_catalog|
+-------------+

+---------+
|namespace|
+---------+
|  default|
|   sparkk|
+---------+

+---------+
|namespace|
+---------+
|  default|
|   sparkk|
+---------+

Note: in Trino with Iceberg connector everything works as expected - I added 3 Iceberg catalogs (fintech, telco, plants), specified the same Hive Metastore URI, and set hive.metastore.thrift.catalog-name=fintech etc. Just trying to replicate same behaviour in Spark.
answer:
Q : Is it possible to use one Hive Metastore with different hive catalogs in Spark (Iceberg)?

Answer : **Nope **

IMHO Spark Catalog Model Is Independent of Hive Metastore Catalog Entries Iceberg Catalog Implementation Doesn’t Create Multiple Spark Catalogs Automatically.. Spark’s Hive Catalog Behavior Is Not the Same as Trino
